newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk telecoms follow stocks up.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk telecoms follow stocks up.

text.p: Prices of high-yield bonds in the telecommunications sector strengthened, while Grand Union Co bonds continued to plummet, in an otherwise quiet day in the U.S. corporate bond market, traders said.
Investment-grade and high-yield bond prices were firm today on extremely low volume, traders said. The thin volume was characteristic of summer Mondays, traders noted.
In the junk bond market, telecommunications sector credits rose 1/2 a point on average, triggered by a surge in the stock prices of those companies on Monday.
"The sector has been oversold recently and buyers started coming back in," said one trader referring to market activity in telecom bonds and equities.

Securities of competitive local exchange carriers (CLECs) weakened following a recent federal court decision that overturned key parts of federal rules designed to open the $100 billion local telephone markets controlled by the regional Baby Bell companies.
But some analysts said the regulations could actually benefit certain CLECs which already had interconnection agreements with Baby Bells.
A Grand Union spokewoman did not immediately return calls.
Elsewhere, bond spreads of Tenet Healthcare Corp ended the day five basis points wider after being quoted as much as 10 basis points wider in the morning.
The spread movement was the result of reports that talks between the company and Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp were temporarily on hold, traders added.
Columbia bonds were unchanged on Monday, they said.
Traders noted neither bond was actively traded on Monday. They predicted both bonds could experience more volatility tomorrow as more investors return to the market.
Two such companies, Brooks Fiber Properties Inc and McLeodUSA Inc were examples of telecommunications issues which strengthened on Monday, traders said.
In other news, Grand Union 12 percent unsecured notes due '04 continued their recent slide as concerns grew that the company would be unable to make an upcoming interest payment.
The bonds of the Wayne, NJ-based supermarket company, closed at 49 1/4-50, after opening the day around 55.
One trader said there is a continuing belief that the company may have to recapitalize in order to avoid liquidity problems.
